solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Back of this vehicle is hit

indicators.note: here the charade joins the end letter and the vehicle side by side
the back of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of this is used

parts.note: last letter of this
a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The rear of a vehicle has been rammed in a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past participle of strike, a direct synonym of the verb hit in the same tense.

clue.text: Bit of stuff on tree that is sticky

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the tree
just a bit, the first letter, of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of stuff
the lime is a tree, the linden

explanation.surface: A piece of gooey matter has got onto a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is any thick, viscous substance, so it is a material that is sticky.

clue.text: Hesitation about hostility brings relief

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
spite is malice or hostility

explanation.surface: Pausing before quarrelling gives a moment of ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or period of rest from something unpleasant, a relief.

clue.text: Able to take part, being given set of holy books

parts.note: to compete is to take part in a contest
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone qualified to join in, being handed scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent means having the necessary skill or capability, the same as capable.

clue.text: Chatter in B&B with wild wind outside

indicators.note: the wind is placed outside, wrapping round the pair of letters from the bed and breakfast

parts.note: a gale is a wild, strong wind
the two Bs of B&B (bed and breakfast)

explanation.surface: Guests at a guesthouse talk away while a storm howls outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To gabble is to talk rapidly and unintelligibly, a form of chattering.

clue.text: Muslim man, holy person among top people

parts.note: Ali is a common Muslim man's name
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A Muslim man and a saint are among the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the group of the most celebrated or important people, celebrities of the first rank.

clue.text: Function in club — old-fashioned headgear required

indicators.note: the function goes inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: At a society's event, period costume hats are compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' and 'club' suggest a social event, but one is maths and the other a sporting bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinet was a light steel medieval helmet, an antique piece of armour for the head.

clue.text: Manners of quite silly communication, ignored first and last

indicators.note: silly signals the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the opening and closing letters are dropped, leaving the middle

parts.note: a letter is a written communication

explanation.surface: Rather foolish correspondence that is rude at the start and finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' turns QUITE into ETIQU; 'ignored first and last' trims LETTER to ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour in society, the conventional rules of good conduct.

clue.text: Be only partially successful? Charming!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as ...: to ... but not all

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split into two words, win some, as in winning some and losing some.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome describes an engaging, attractive manner, which is what charming means.

clue.text: Hide children — not entirely compassionate

parts.note: kids are children

indicators.note: the word is not given whole, so its final letter is cut off

parts.note: kind means compassionate

explanation.surface: A command to conceal the youngsters, from someone not wholly sympathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidskin is leather made from the skin of a young goat, and a hide is an animal skin.

clue.text: Money given to crusade in hub location?

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, a piece of money
a rally is a mass gathering for a cause, a campaign or crusade

explanation.surface: Cash donated to a campaign at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrally is an adverb meaning at the centre, the hub being the central point.

clue.text: Degradation of fellows on row being held by detective

indicators.note: the detective word holds the other letters inside it
in an across clue, fellows on row puts the fellows after the row

parts.note: a file is a row or line of people
fellows are men

explanation.surface: A detective investigates men in a row as part of some degrading affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Defilement is the act of making something impure or corrupt, a kind of debasement or degradation.

clue.text: A word from holy woman about love

indicators.note: the holy woman goes around the zero letter

parts.note: a nun is a holy woman
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Some kind words from a nun on the subject of love.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is a word class, so a noun is, quite literally, a word of one grammatical type.

clue.text: Island in secret escape

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the next two words

parts.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A clandestine flight to an island, as in a wartime story.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island in the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Vehicle second-rate — to member of family it is a gem

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
B grade means second-rate
an uncle is a member of the family

explanation.surface: An inferior car, but an uncle regards it as a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, especially a garnet cut in a rounded shape.

clue.text: Document showing overturned vehicle by gallery

indicators.note: the gallery stands beside the vehicle, after it
an overturned cart is upside down, so its letters read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Paperwork about a cart toppled over next to an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractate is a treatise or formal written essay, a type of document.

clue.text: Answer to snake bite in vain with ten in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed, so they are rearranged

parts.note: letters for rearranging
letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: Treating a snake bite fails, with ten people in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Answer' looks like A, but the whole phrase 'Answer to snake bite' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antivenin is an antidote serum against venom, the remedy for a snake's bite.

clue.text: Maiden entering to make a light meal

indicators.note: the maiden letter goes into the word for making

parts.note: to create is to make
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman steps in to prepare a light snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is an afternoon refreshment of scones and tea, a small snack rather than a full dinner.

clue.text: A theologian, one disciple who was an essayist

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
one is the Roman numeral I
a son can be a follower or disciple, as in a son of a master

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion and one follower who wrote essays.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was an English essayist, co-founder of The Spectator magazine in 1711.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was a famous English writer of essays, chiefly for The Spectator.

clue.text: Mark's daughter wearing a hat

indicators.note: the hat is worn, so it goes around the daughter letter

parts.note: tile is old British slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A man called Mark has a daughter in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, a written mark. 'Tile' is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy diacritic sign placed over letters such as the Spanish n.

clue.text: Get to understand security device is secure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grasp or catch on to an idea
second meaning, read literally: the latch is on, so the door is fastened

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read as a little scene: when the latch is on, the door is held fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To latch on is an informal idiom meaning to grasp or comprehend something.

clue.text: Fish mostly of a red hue

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour

explanation.surface: A fish that is largely reddish in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a European freshwater fish of the carp family, with red fins.

clue.text: One gripped by religious freedom drooling

indicators.note: the numeral is held within the religious word

parts.note: salvation is deliverance from sin, a religious freeing
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A believer seized by spiritual liberation is left slobbering.
explanation.definitionFit: Salivation is the production of spit, so it describes the act of drooling.

clue.text: Shrine put up, protected by religious organisation

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the organisation's letters

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the word put, turned round

explanation.surface: A shrine erected under the care of a church body.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupa is a domed Buddhist monument housing relics, a type of shrine.

clue.text: Beastly noises all right outside home? Start to scream

indicators.note: the OK goes outside, around the home word

parts.note: OK means all right
in means at home

indicators.note: the start, the first letter, of the following word

parts.note: first letter of scream

explanation.surface: Fine animal sounds outdoors, then a shriek starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinks are the grunting sounds of pigs, so literally the noises of beasts.

clue.text: Represents dramatically as cast maybe

parts.note: cast is the letters of ACTS rearranged, with OUT as the signal for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A cast performing a play, presenting it on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the letters of ACTS sent out of order give CAST, which is why 'as cast maybe' clues it.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a scene is to perform or portray it theatrically.

clue.text: What's silly can then delight

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are muddled into nonsense and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something foolish can then turn out to be charming.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm and please them greatly, a synonym of the verb delight.

clue.text: Group of nine chaps heading off with drunken dean

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: a drunken dean staggers, so his letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nine men set off with a tipsy college dean.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a set of nine, from the Greek word for that number.

clue.text: Items of fruit — yellow fruits, not black

indicators.note: not signals the black letter is taken away

parts.note: bananas are yellow fruits
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A fruit bowl with yellow fruit, but none that have turned black.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is another name for pineapples, the tropical fruit.
